record.original_question: Let p = 2 and G_{2n} = GL_{2n}(F_2). Is the degree-n homology group H_n(G_{2n}; F_2) one-dimensional over F_2 and generated by the determinant class det_n arising from the maximal elementary 2-subgroup A_{n,n}?

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 Is Hn(G2n; F2) = F2 generated by detn ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p=2$ and let $G_{2n} = \mathrm{GL}_{2n}(\mathbb{F}_2)$ denote the general linear group of $2n\times 2n$ invertible matrices over the field with two elements. Inside $G_{2n}$, consider the elementary abelian $2$-subgroup
$$A_{n,n} = \left\{ \begin{pmatrix} I_n & X \\ 0 & I_n \end{pmatrix} : X \in M_n(\mathbb{F}_2) \right\} \cong (\mathbb{F}_2)^{n^2},$$
which is a maximal elementary abelian $2$-subgroup of $G_{2n}$ of rank $n^2$. Working with mod-$2$ group homology, the inclusion $A_{n,n}\hookrightarrow G_{2n}$ induces a map on homology. Let $\det_n \in H_n(G_{2n};\mathbb{F}_2)$ denote the "determinant class," defined as the image under this induced map of the top exterior product class $e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n$ associated with the determinant polynomial in $H^*(A_{n,n};\mathbb{F}_2)$ (equivalently, the class detecting the determinant invariant in degree $n$).

Question: Is $H_n(G_{2n};\mathbb{F}_2)$ a one-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_2$-vector space, generated by the class $\det_n$?
